data.title: Japan Core Machinery Orders Sink 3.7% In July
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - The total value of core machinery orders in Japan was down a seasonally adjusted 3.7 percent on month in July, the Cabinet Office said on Wednesday - coming in at 1.016 trillion yen.

That missed expectations for a decline of 1.2 percent following the 9.7 percent increase in June.

On a yearly basis, orders climbed 11.2 percent - again shy of expectations for a gain of 15.3 percent and down from 16.9 percent in the previous month.

For the third quarter of 2026, orders are forecast to rise 4.9 percent on quarter and 19.9 percent on year.

The total value of machinery orders received by 280 manufacturers operating in Japan decreased by 5.5 percent on month but surged 36.8 percent on year to 4.195 trillion yen.

data.title: CME hog futures set contract lows; cattle down on profit-taking
data.description:
By Julie Ingwersen

Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) lean hog futures hit life-of-contract lows on Tuesday, pressured by ample U.S. hog supplies and slumping wholesale pork prices, analysts said.

CME October lean hog futures (LHV26) settled down 0.525 cent at 79.075 cents per pound after notching a contract low at 78.875 cents, and December hogs (LHZ26) ended down 1.600 cents at 69.650 cents after posting a contract low at 69.500 cents.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture quoted the wholesale pork carcass cutout on Tuesday afternoon at $87.50 per hundredweight, down $2.28 from Monday and the lowest reading since February 2024.

"The cutout value is the lowest it's been in quite a while," said Doug Houghton, analyst at Brock Associates. Demand for pork in the wholesale market "keeps getting squeezed by big supplies of low-priced chicken, and beef demand from retailers is pretty stubborn," Houghton said.

Meanwhile, CME live cattle futures also ended lower, but prices were coming off one-month highs set during the session. Cattle futures drew underlying support from tight U.S. cattle supplies and expectations for steady to stronger cash cattle trades this week.

CME October live cattle futures settled down 1.550 cents at 220.700 cents per pound, retreating after posting a one-month high at 222.825 cents, and December cattle ended down 1.800 cents at 223.350 cents.

CME October feeder cattle finished down 4 cents at 333.850 cents per pound.

Traders were likely also adjusting positions ahead of Friday's monthly USDA Cattle on Feed report, Houghton said. Analysts surveyed by Reuters expected the government to report the number of cattle in U.S. feedlots as of September 1 at 11.268 million head, up 1.7% from a year ago.

However, the poll showed placements into feedlots and marketings in August were lower than a year ago.

data.title: Nissan to build new hybrid SUV model for Europe at its UK plant
data.description:
By Nick Carey

Japanese automaker Nissan said on Wednesday it would build a new hybrid small SUV for Europe at its UK plant in Sunderland and would invest £170 million ($229 million) to assemble it there.

The company said the Kicks e-POWER hybrid would be made in Sunderland alongside the Qashqai, Juke and electric Leaf models, but it did not provide a timeline for production.

Nissan has been restructuring to slash costs by ditching plants, cutting jobs and shelving some future models, including the electric version of the Qashqai.

There have been concerns over the future of the Sunderland plant, which is Britain's largest car assembly plant.

Nissan said in June it was exploring renting out one of the two production lines at Sunderland to rapidly-expanding Chinese automaker Chery to build cars there.

Reuters reported later that month that the British government was in advanced talks with Nissan about providing it financial support in return for a long-term commitment and investment in Sunderland.

"The decision to build this new model in Sunderland is a huge vote of confidence in the UK's manufacturing expertise and automotive future," Britain's business minister Jonathan Reynolds said in a statement.

($1 = 0.7422 pounds)

data.description: Gold's descent continues in early Asian trade as expectations of central bank tightening to fight inflation dim the appeal of non-yielding assets. data.title: S.F. Holding to Raise Nearly $1.50 Bln Through Yuan Bonds
data.description:
By Megan Cheah

S.F. Holding plans to raise nearly $1.50 billion through the sale of yuan-denominated bonds.

The Chinese logistics service provider is issuing the guaranteed notes in two tranches worth 5.0 billion yuan each, equivalent to $744.8 million, it said Wednesday.

One of the tranches will consist of bonds due 2029 carrying a 1.75% coupon, it said. The other will comprise notes due 2031 with a 1.85% coupon.

The company intends to use the net proceeds from the bond issuance for refinancing and general corporate purposes, it said. Its Shenzhen-listed shares closed 0.3% higher at 31.08 yuan on Tuesday, while Hong Kong-listed shares last ended down 1.1%.

HSBC and ICBC International are among financial institutions advising S.F. Holding's bond issuance.

More Chinese companies are tapping Hong Kong's market as they seek different capital pools to fund operations via share offerings and bond issuances. Hong Kong is widely seen as a gateway for foreign investors to allocate capital to Chinese assets, given the hurdles foreign capital faces in accessing the country's onshore markets.

Z.AI said on Sunday it plans to raise more than $5.0 billion through a share placement and zero-coupon convertible bonds to fuel its artificial-intelligence investments.

data.title: Talga Group Signs European Anode Supply LOI with EAS Batteries for Vittangi Project
data.description:
Talga Group has signed a non-binding Anode Supply Letter of Intent with German manufacturer EAS Batteries GmbH to establish a strategic supply of graphite anode material from its mine-to-battery Vittangi anode project in Sweden.

The LOI sets a structured pathway through product testing and qualification towards a proposed five-year supply agreement covering Talga’s Talnode anode products for EAS’s high-power lithium-ion (Li-ion) battery manufacturing.

Talga and EAS plan to finalise product specifications and quality requirements while completing supply-chain, human rights, and environmental due diligence including requirements covering carbon dioxide footprint and ESG metrics.

The parties are targeting April 2027 to negotiate and agree a binding terms sheet, with the aim of executing a definitive Supply Agreement by July 2027 or a later date agreed between them.

Progressing to a binding arrangement would establish EAS as a long-term Talnode customer, expand Talga’s customer base in the high-performance battery segment and strengthen its position within the European battery value chain.

Qualification and Commercial Path

The proposed supply agreement would carry extension potential and a mutually agreed euro-denominated pricing mechanism, while the potential volumes to be supplied remain under discussion between the parties.

Both sides have also agreed to provide reasonable strategic support to each other’s project financing processes as they work through qualification and the steps needed to reach a definitive commercial arrangement.

“Talga’s natural graphite battery anode products deliver high power and high performance with traceable supply chains—attributes increasingly underpinning procurement policies in Europe and elsewhere, especially those companies serving industries such as defence and aerospace,” chief executive officer Martin Phillips said.

“A resilient European battery industry requires strong regional supply chains,” EAS general manager Michael Deutmeyer added.

“Talga’s planned European anode production aligns well with our commitment to developing high-performance battery cells while strengthening local value creation and supply security”.

European Battery Supply Focus

EAS has more than 30 years of experience producing custom large-format cylindrical cells and battery systems for demanding applications across the maritime, aerospace, defence, automotive, and industrial sectors.

The German manufacturer combines cell design, pilot-to-series production capabilities, and battery system integration, and is focused on building end-to-end Li-ion cell production based on a European supply chain.

For EAS and its German and European customers, a binding supply agreement would provide long-term access to Talga anode material produced in Europe while supporting local value creation and supply security.

Talga considers a multi-year offtake with a German manufacturer capable of strengthening the commercial foundations of both parties and supporting access to German and European Union funding programs.

data.title: Latest Survey by U.S.-Based Herbalife Shows Taiwan Ranks Among Asia Pacific Leaders in Health Awareness Willing to Invest in Health, Yet Struggling to Stay Consistent
data.description:
TAIPEI, Sept. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As health awareness continues to rise, pursuing a healthier lifestyle has become a growing trend among the people across generations. However, incorporating healthy habits into daily life and maintaining them over the long term remains a common challenge for many. Herbalife, a global health and wellness company, community, and platform, has released its latest "2026 Asia Pacific Health Culture Survey", providing an in-depth analysis of health awareness and barriers to taking action among consumers across Asia Pacific and Taiwan. Conducted in May 2026, the survey covered more than 10,000 respondents across 11 markets, including Australia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

The survey found that nearly nine in ten people in Taiwan are concerned about their personal health and preventive care, placing overall health awareness among the leading markets in Asia Pacific. More than 65% of consumers also indicated that they are willing to invest more resources in their health.[1] However, a high level of health awareness does not necessarily translate into sustained action, with nearly half (44%) of respondents in Taiwan admitting that a "lack of motivation" is a key barrier preventing them from turning awareness into consistent action. In response, Herbalife encourages people to establish an "active lifestyle" through three core strategies—balanced nutrition, regular physical activity, and support from in-person communities—to help people in Taiwan incorporate healthy actions into their daily lives and gradually develop long-term, sustainable healthy habits.

Decoding Asia Pacific Health Trends: Nearly 90% of Taiwanese Demonstrate High Health Awareness, Ranking Among the Top in Asia Pacific. Age and Health Warnings Prompt Greater Concern, with Weight Management Emerging as the Most Urgent Need

The latest "2026 Asia Pacific Health Culture Survey" found that 89% of people in Taiwan demonstrate a high level of health awareness (higher than the Asia Pacific average of 82%). More than 70% of respondents also said they pay greater attention to their health than they did three years ago. The top two reasons driving people in Taiwan to pay greater attention to their health are "getting older" (48%) and "personal health warnings" (43%), indicating that as people age and experience occasional changes in their physical condition, they are becoming more aware that their health is not as it once was and are therefore taking a more proactive approach to health management. The survey further found that among various physical health indicators, "weight management" is considered the most critical and urgent health priority, with as many as 35% of Taiwanese respondents identifying it as the area they most urgently need to improve—ranking first among the 11 Asia Pacific markets surveyed.

65% of Taiwanese Willing to Invest More in Their Health! Supplements and Exercise Most Preferred, Yet as Many as 44% Struggle to Stay Consistent Due to "Lack of Motivation"

The survey found that more than 65% of consumers in Taiwan are willing to invest more resources in their health. As many as 47% of Taiwanese respondents selected "using nutritional supplements" as their top choice for daily health maintenance (ranking first in Asia Pacific), followed by regular exercise (46%) and healthy eating (42%). However, health management cannot be achieved overnight. Overly intense or short-term, sprint-style changes are often difficult to maintain over the long term. Incorporating healthy actions into daily life is the key to developing lasting healthy habits.

The research shows that although younger generations (Gen Z) are more proactive in trying health-related activities than they were three years ago, only around 30% are able to "stay consistent" and maintain these habits, significantly lower than the nearly 50% among older generations. In addition, as many as 44% of Taiwanese respondents identified "lack of motivation" as the biggest obstacle (ranking second in Asia Pacific). These findings highlight that while people in Taiwan generally place a high value on health and are willing to invest resources in it, turning that commitment into sustainable daily habits remains a challenge that urgently needs to be addressed.

The key factor behind younger generations' difficulty in maintaining healthy habits over the long term may be a lack of support and companionship. Compared with other age groups, Gen Z has a greater need for the motivation provided by "community and peer support." Through getting together with others to check in and engaging in interactive support, integrating personal health management into social interactions can help narrow the gap between awareness and actual action, allowing healthy habits to be maintained over the long term.

Building an Active Lifestyle Through Balanced Nutrition, Regular Exercise, and Community Support

As health awareness continues to grow, the lifestyles of people in Taiwan are gradually changing. Herbalife recognizes that maintaining overall health requires long-term commitment and consistency, while science-based nutrition solutions, personalized guidance, and supportive communities are all important foundations for helping people establish healthy habits. In fact, pursuing a healthy lifestyle does not require drastic, life-changing adjustments, but can instead be achieved gradually through three core strategies:

  • Balanced Nutrition (Simplifying Daily Nutritional Intake): Build a foundation of high-quality, balanced nutrition. Rather than setting strict or extreme dietary plans from the outset, start with small goals and gradually develop healthy eating habits.
  • Regular Exercise (Incorporating Small Actions into Daily Life): Begin with light, low-pressure physical activities in daily life. Incorporate "micro-exercises" such as walking, stretching, and taking the stairs into everyday routines to establish regular exercise habits without adding pressure.
  • Building Community Support and a Supportive Environment: Invite like-minded friends or family members to exercise together and participate in health check-ins. Through reminders, sharing progress, and positive encouragement, healthy habits can become part of social life and a more enjoyable experience.

[1] 2024 Herbalife Asia Pacific Health Business Survey

data.title: Hanwha Power Obtains ABS Approval in Principle for 22,000 CBM LNG Bunkering Vessel Concept Design
data.description:
• Jointly participated in GASTECH 2026 with Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Engines, showcasing the Group's integrated marine and energy solutions.
  • Applied multi-cargo technology for LNG and ammonia, along with a hybrid electric propulsion system.
  • Strengthened the competitiveness of an integrated engineering and procurement package by incorporating the Group's core technologies.

SEOUL, South Korea, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hanwha Power announced on September 15 that it has obtained Approval in Principle (AiP) from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) for the concept design of a 22,000-cubic-meter LNG bunkering vessel at GASTECH 2026, the world's largest gas and energy exhibition, held in Bangkok, Thailand.

At GASTECH 2026, Hanwha Power operated a joint booth with major marine and energy affiliates, including Hanwha Ocean and Hanwha Engines, showcasing comprehensive marine solutions from eco-friendly vessel transitions and propulsion systems to marine equipment and related technologies.

The certificate presentation ceremony was held on September 15 local time, attended by Hanwha Power Marine Solution Business Division Head Hoon-min Kim, Vice President Jong-kyu Hwang, who oversees Technical Solutions, and key ABS representatives.

With this AiP, Hanwha Power has completed its lineup of medium- and large-scale LNG bunkering vessels, ranging from 7,500 to 22,000 CBM.

A key feature is the design's LNG-ammonia multi-cargo capability, enabling transport of both LNG and ammonia, an emerging next-generation clean fuel. The design incorporates high-manganese steel cargo containment technology, Mc-CⓇ, allowing adaptation to future alternative fuels with minimal modifications, providing shipowners greater long-term flexibility and competitiveness.

Given bunkering vessels' coastal operating profile, Hanwha Power applied a hybrid electric propulsion system integrating Onshore Power Supply (OPS) with an Energy Storage System (ESS). This minimizes harmful emissions while berthed or operating in coastal areas, while improving operational efficiency and economic performance.

Hanwha Power also incorporated Group core technologies, including dual-fuel generator sets, ESS, Electrical Power System integration, Integrated Automation System, and Cargo Handling System. By integrating these, the company aims to maximize competitiveness and synergies of its integrated Engineering and Procurement (EP) package.

"This ABS AiP marks another important milestone demonstrating Hanwha Power's technological reliability and commercial viability in the global eco-friendly vessel market," said Hoon-min Kim, Head of Hanwha Power's Marine Solution Business Division. "Building on Hanwha Group's differentiated clean-technology capabilities, we will continue to provide global shipowners with optimized integrated solutions for the transition to more sustainable marine transportation."

data.title: Brookfield Agrees to US$2.9 Billion Acquisition of Australia's Reliance
data.description:
By Stuart Condie

SYDNEY--Brookfield Asset Management agreed to acquire Reliance Worldwide in an all-cash deal that values the plumbing-supplies manufacturer at US$2.9 billion.

Australia-listed Reliance, which operates domestically and in countries such as the U.S., Canada and Mexico, on Wednesday said Brookfield firmed its US$3.38-a-share proposal after four weeks of exclusive due diligence.

Reliance said its directors unanimously recommended the offer to shareholders, who could opt to receive U.S. dollars or 4.75 Australian dollars a share.

The stock was at A$4.33 ahead of Wednesday's open.

Brookfield viewed Reliance as a global, market-leading industrial company with value creation opportunities, said Anuj Ranjan, chief executive of Brookfield's private-equity group.

"Brookfield's global operating expertise in industrials and the U.S. housing ecosystem positions us well to support Reliance in its next phase of growth and over the long term," Ranjan said.

data.title: TMX Group Prices $1.1 Billion Private Placement Debenture Offering
data.description:
TORONTO, ON, Sept 16, 2026 - (ACN Newswire) - TMX Group Limited ("TMX Group") today announced that it has priced a Canadian private placement offering (the "Offering") of $1.1 billion aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured debentures (collectively, the "Debentures") to accredited investors in Canada comprising: (i) C$250 million aggregate principal amount of 3.862% Series K Senior Unsecured Debentures due September 26, 2028; (ii) C$400 million aggregate principal amount of 4.571% Series L Senior Unsecured Debentures due September 22, 2033; and (iii) C$450 million aggregate principal amount of 4.904% Series M Senior Unsecured Debentures due September 23, 2036. The Debentures will be direct senior unsecured and unsubordinated obligations of TMX Group and will rank pari passu with all other senior unsecured and unsubordinated indebtedness of TMX Group.

TMX Group expects the Offering to close on September 22, 2026 and the Debentures are expected to receive a credit rating of "AA (Low)" with a Stable Trend from DBRS Limited.

The net proceeds from the Offering will be used to repay a portion of outstanding indebtedness and for general corporate purposes.

The Debentures are being offered exclusively to persons in a Canadian province through a syndicate of agents led by National Bank of Canada Capital Markets and TD Securities and including RBC Capital Markets, BMO Capital Markets, CIBC Capital Markets, Scotiabank, Barclays, Canaccord Genuity, Casgrain & Company Limited, Cedar Leaf Capital Inc., and Citigroup Global Markets Canada Inc., on a private placement basis in reliance upon exemptions from the prospectus requirements under applicable securities laws in those provinces. The Debentures have not been qualified for sale to the public under such securities laws.

This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy the Debentures or any other securities of TMX Group in any jurisdiction, and is not an offer for sale within the United States of any securities of TMX Group. Accordingly, the Debentures may not be offered or sold in the United States except in certain transactions exempt from the registration requirements under applicable U.S. securities laws.
